item.title: Free Watch Party: USA vs Belgium
item.description:
Monday, July 6, 2026 at 5:30 PM

The first knock out round is over and the field has been cut in half. Every match from here is win or go home, and tonight someone’s World Cup journey ends. The Round of 16 is knockout soccer at its most raw and thrilling. Be here for it! Festival gates open at 5:30 p.m. to the sounds of DJ Athenz. Kickoff is at 7:00 p.m. Admission is free! Food and Beverage Concessions: Enjoy a variety of festival food fare, beer and wine, and non-alcoholic beverages from Coca-Cola. Visit Smalls Sliders for burgers, fries, and shakes, stop by Franky’s for a gourmet hot dog or sausage, and cool down with Frios Gourmet Pops. Stop by Hearsay’s festival tent for a cold beer or beer bucket or grab a michelada, wine, or beer from Gaspacho’s festival tent. Non-alcoholic drinks from Coca-Cola as well as pre-packaged snacks can be purchased at the Community Partner Concessions Booth, proceeds benefiting Levy Park and the event’s community partners. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Community Partners: Supporting this event is the Japan-America Society of Houston. The Japan-America Society of Houston (JASH) is the leading organization that connects Houston’s diverse community, local businesses, and individuals to advance the mutual interest of American and Japanese peoples. JASH programs in language and education, arts and culture, and business initiatives and networking provide opportunities for collaboration and important people-to-people exchange. JASH hosts a monthly program at Levy Park: Japan Junction, as well as seasonal programming throughout the year. All proceeds from the Community Partner Concessions booth will support JASH and Levy Park. Face Painting & Henna Art: Get into the tournament spirit with face and body art from Gio’s Art Kreations and Henna Station & Glitter Bar Merchandise: Event merchandise celebrating Houston, Levy Park, and the global soccer tournament will also be available for purchase. Art Installations and Photo Opportunities: Commemorate the experience with a photo tour of the park, including life-sized soccer-themed photo backdrops and a tournament bracket. Visit our soccer ball music box and turn the crank for festive sounds. Festival Guidelines: VISITORS MUST COMPLY WITH DIRECTIONS FROM PARK PERSONNEL, OR THEY WILL BE ASKED TO LEAVE THE PARK. PARENTS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR CHILDREN’S SAFETY IN THE PARK. CHAIRS AND SEATING: No outside furniture. Blankets may be brought into the Festival site for the designated blanket seating area. All other furniture is available on a first-come, first-served basis. STROLLERS & WAGONS: Oversized strollers and wagons may need to be parked in a designated area during the festival. All visitors must comply with park personnel regarding stroller and wagon parking. FOOD AND BEVERAGES: Guests are permitted to enter with one factory-sealed bottle of water. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Other outside food and drinks are prohibited (exceptions will be made for baby food and necessary medical dietary food items). A variety of food, non-alcoholic drinks, beer, and wine will be available for purchase from Festival concessionaires. RE-ENTRY: If you leave the Festival site, you will be re-screened before re-entry. THE FOLLOWING ARE PROHIBITED: Smoking or Vaping Umbrellas Drug Use Kites and Drones Recreational Motorized Vehicles Guns, knives, any weaponry Soliciting Bikes, scooters, rollerblades, and roller skates

item.title: What AI, Cybersecurity, and Tequila Have in Common.
item.description:
Tuesday, July 7, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://luma.com/0rfy7te0 Most companies treat AI like a shortcut to growth: it delivers immediate results, but the long-term operational fallout is brutal. ​Everyone is caught up in the rush, plugging automated tools into critical infrastructure without checking the foundation. But speed without security isn’t progress, it’s an open invitation for cyber threats. It’s time to face the structural reality. ​Join Blue People and Alpfa Houston for an unfiltered session with Reynaldo Gonzalez, an industry veteran with 18+ years of experience securing critical infrastructure. ​The Realities We’re Breaking Down: ​AI doesn’t change the value of knowledge; it changes the value of curiosity. The ultimate security edge belongs to leaders who know how to ask the right questions, not just trust the output. ​Your biggest competitive advantage is becoming more human, not less. In a world of automated systems, human judgment and sharp intuition remain the only truly un-hackable firewalls left. ​AI is the greatest operational amplifier ever created. It scales your wins, but it weaponizes your internal flaws. If your baseline security is weak, AI just helps you fail faster and at scale. ​The single biggest risk today isn’t AI, it’s human complacency. The danger isn’t rogue technology or advanced malware; it’s our own blind trust in automated workflows. ​Stop operating on hope. Turn cyber resilience into your unfair advantage. ​📅 July 7th, 2026 | 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM 📍 The Ion Houston Hosted by Blue People & Alpfa Houston ​👉 Ask about our parking options at the end of the event!

Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: Frame of Reference in UAV Search and Rescue: Exocentric vs. Egocentric View for Navigation, Target Detection, and Collision Awareness
item.description:
Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 4 PM

  Speaker: Yining Zhang Masters Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Psychology Unmanned Aerial Systems (UASs) have enabled search-and-rescue (SAR) missions to be safer, more efficient, and more effective due to their advanced mobility and sensing technologies. Traditionally, UASs employ a first-person, egocentric frame of reference (FOR), enabled by the camera system installed on the vehicle. However, this FOR provides limited visibility of the vehicle's surrounding environment, leading to blind spots. In contrast, research has shown that an exocentric, behind-the-vehicle FOR can lead to better mission outcomes and safer teleoperation. The current study compared operator performance and eye-movement patterns using the egocentric and exocentric FORs in a simulated SAR mission. A total of 37 participants performed three tasks using the two FORs, including collision-awareness, route-deviation detection, and target-detection tasks. The results showed that the effectiveness of the FORs was dependent on the task specifications. For the collision-awareness and target-detection tasks, there was no significant difference in response time (RT) or hit rate (H). For the route-deviation detection task, participants exhibited a speed-accuracy trade-off: they had a faster RT but lower H in the exocentric condition compared to the egocentric condition. Additionally, we found that participants in the exocentric condition attributed more visual attention to the camera view than in the egocentric condition, potentially due to the high salience of the vehicle body against the surrounding environment. Overall, the current study suggested that future UASs should employ a dynamic visual display, allowing the operator to choose the FOR that is more appropriate for the mission. https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/94483800467?pwd=XgoaQZA7ioB8HHGavYPyGnaDag6iDl.1 (Department : Psychology)

June 10: “The Tubmaker Who Flew to the Sea” and Teru Teru Bozu paper craft June in Japan is known as Tsuyu, the rainy season, when gentle rains and cloudy skies become a part of daily life. But what do you do when you are hoping for sunny weather before an important day? In Japan, people often hang Teru Teru Bozu, a traditional handmade decoration believed to bring good weather. Usually made from tissue paper or cloth, these cheerful little figures are displayed near windows or doors to wish for sunshine. Join us for a kamishibai reading of “Okeya no Ten Nobori” or “The Tubmaker Who Flew to the Sky,” a whimsical tale featuring a sleepy thunder god, Kaminari-sama, whose storms bring rainy weather. item.title: K-Nexus: Hierarchical Gene-to-Cell AI Modeling for Perturbation-Induced Transcriptomic Shift Recovery
item.description:
Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 5 PM

  Speaker: Zihan Zhao Masters Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Electrical and Computer Engineering Predicting cellular responses to genetic and chemical perturbations can accelerate therapeutic discovery by reducing experimental screening. However, predicting post-perturbation gene expression, particularly for unseen perturbations, remains challenging because response signals are sparse, cellular responses are heterogeneous and often unpaired, and responsive genes are obscured by dominant non-responsive genes. We propose K-Nexus, a hierarchical gene-to-cell framework that formulates perturbation response prediction as distribution-shift recovery over responsive genes. K-Nexus encodes perturbation-conditioned regulatory interactions at the gene level and aggregates them into cell-level representations that preserve response heterogeneity. Attention-based gene importance, response-aware weighting, and group-based distributional training focus learning on genes driving perturbation-induced changes. K-Nexus also incorporates perturbation and regulatory graphs to capture functional relationships between targeted genes and downstream pathways. Across three single-cell perturbation benchmarks, K-Nexus outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, particularly in responsive-gene distributional alignment, demonstrating improved recovery of expression shifts and generalization to unseen perturbations.   (Department : Electrical and Computer Engineering)

item.title: O⁺ Transport from the Ionospheric Cusp to the Inner Magnetosphere: A Global MHD and Test Particle Study
item.description:
Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: Herman Brown Hall

  Speaker: Yiwen Zhu Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Herman Brown Hall HBH 254 During geomagnetic storms, ionospheric oxygen (O⁺) can become a significant constituent of Earth's ring current, the current system whose buildup drives the main-phase depression of the surface magnetic field. The polar cusp is a principal source, feeding O⁺ outflow into the magnetotail lobe, but how much of this oxygen is delivered inward to the inner magnetosphere, and how it is energized along the way, remain poorly quantified, in part because the transport spans scales that no single model resolves.   In this thesis, we follow ionospheric oxygen from the cusp to the ring current using a global magnetohydrodynamic simulation (GAMERA/MAGE) coupled one-way to a test-particle tracer (CHIMP). Because MAGE includes an inner-magnetosphere model, it produces and resolves the mesoscale bursty bulk flows (BBFs) of the plasma sheet that drive earthward transport. With it, we identify a "drop-down" channel that controls the delivery to the inner magnetosphere: the dipolarization field carried by these flows pulls cusp oxygen from the lobe down to the equatorial plasma sheet, and the ions that experience it form a more efficient ring-current injection channel than those that convect down the tail unaided. Within an adiabatic (guiding-center) framework, we decompose the energy gain along the transport into its Fermi, betatron, and E×B contributions and quantify each, and we characterize where the oxygen departs from adiabatic behavior. To put these results on a quantitative footing, we weight the test particles by an O⁺ outflow rate computed directly from the simulation's MHD variables. For a real storm, this lets us quantify the absolute amount of cusp oxygen delivered to the inner magnetosphere and follow its contribution to the ring current through the storm, showing that a portion of the cusp oxygen is accelerated to ring-current energies and adds to the ring-current population. As a separate diagnostic, we characterize the energy and pitch-angle phase-space distributions, f(K, α), of the cusp oxygen at several locations along the transport and at ring-current entry, mapping how the population is energized and reshaped as it moves inward. Finally, we step back to the cusp itself. Forecasting where the cusp lies from the upstream solar wind is operationally important, yet no data-driven model has provided the cusp position directly. We develop a machine-learning model, gradient-boosted decision trees trained on DMSP spacecraft cusp crossings, that predicts the cusp location from solar-wind and interplanetary-magnetic-field conditions, offering a fast alternative to a full simulation. Together, these results advance two distinct fronts. The simulation and test-particle study closes a missing link in the cusp-to-ring-current pathway: it resolves how cusp oxygen reaches the inner magnetosphere, decomposes how the ions are energized along the way, and quantifies their absolute contribution to the storm-time ring current. The cusp machine-learning model is a separate, data-driven product: a fast predictor of the cusp location from the upstream solar wind, suited to operational use where a full simulation is impractical. Both improve how the entry of ionospheric heavy ions into the inner magnetosphere can be modeled and anticipated. (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: Buying and Selling Businesses
item.description:
Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 5:30 PM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 029 – 030, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Join Lenny Saizan, owner of Murphy Business & Financial – Southwest Houston, Managing Director of Urban Capital Network, and creator of the Legacy Maximizer exit strategy, for a practical, real-world discussion on selling and buying businesses. Selling or acquiring a business is one of the most significant financial decisions most entrepreneurs will ever make, yet many owners and buyers go through the process for the first time without a clear roadmap. This session breaks down the transaction process from both sides of the table and highlights how thoughtful planning, proper valuation, and coordinated advice can materially impact outcomes. For business owners, the discussion centers on how to maximize enterprise value, prepare for a future exit, and align business decisions with personal wealth, tax, and legacy goals. For buyers, the session explores entrepreneurship through acquisition, including how buying an existing business can reduce risk, generate immediate cash flow, and serve as a growth strategy for current operators. Drawing on his experience as a business broker, investment advisor, and financial professional, Lenny connects the technical aspects of M&A with broader exit planning and wealth strategy considerations, helping attendees understand not just how transactions work, but how they fit into a bigger financial picture. Topics include: Current market conditions and buyer demand When to prepare to sell or buy Key drivers of business value How businesses are valued in the real world Recasting and normalizing financial statements Overview of the sales and acquisition process The role of advisors and the deal team Tax, insurance, and planning considerations before and after a transaction This session is ideal for business owners considering a sale now or in the future, prospective buyers exploring acquisition, and professionals who support small business owners through growth and transition. Presenter Lenny Saizan is the owner and lead broker of Murphy Business & Financial – Southwest Houston, where he advises business owners on exit planning, value maximization, and business sales, and supports buyers pursuing acquisitions and franchises. He is also the co-founder and Managing Director of Urban Capital Network, an investment firm focused on expanding access to private investment opportunities. Earlier in his career, Lenny spent two decades in engineering, automation, and oil and gas, leading teams across operational controls, financial controls, and audit. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from Louisiana State University and an MBA from Tulane University. His credentials include Certified Mergers & Acquisition Professional, Six Sigma Green Belt, and Project Management Professional. In 2025, he was recognized as Deal Maker of The Year at Houston Dealmakers conference.

Blackbird Ordinary. Meet new people. Laugh at hilarious dating stories. Join the conversation. Ladies drink free during showtime 9-10:30 PM. A fun night out where people happen to meet. Wingman Wednesdays is Miami’s social comedy show where dating, relationships, and modern romance become the night’s entertainment. Hosted by Miami’s Best Comedian Manny Garavito and Miami’s Best Master of Ceremonies Luke Prince, the show stirs up live comedy, tasteful crowd interaction, audience stories, terrible dating advice, red flags, green flags, first dates on the spot, and the hilarious realities of navigating Miami’s social scene. Whether you’re single, taken, in the alphabet, somewhere in between, or just here to watch the tea spill, you’ll be part of a night filled with laughs, unexpected moments, and real conversations. Audience participation is encouraged but never required, making it just as fun to watch as it is to jump in. Bring your friends, your situationships, your worst dating stories, but most importantly your sense of humor. Ladies drink free during showtime from 9:00 PM to 10:30 PM. Comedy. Cocktails. Questionable decisions. Topics include but are not limited to: Brickell finance bros Yacht season Sugar daddy retirement plans Instagram followers “What do you do?” stress tests Penthouse with air matresses Dating apps Gym culture Plastic surgery Spiritual girls How to Ghost 101 Toxic Green Flags …And enough unsolicited dating advice to keep everyone single a little longer. Come watch. Come participate. Or just sit back and enjoy the turbulence. Ticket Options General Admission (FREE: frist come, first serve)First come, first served. item.title: Free Watch Party: France vs Morocco
item.description:
Thursday, July 9, 2026 at 1:30 PM

The group stage drama is behind us — now it’s pure knockout soccer. Eight teams left standing, and tonight France and Morocco go to war for a spot in the semifinals. Come feel the electricity. Kickoff is at 3:00 p.m. Admission is free! Food and Beverage Concessions: Enjoy a variety of festival food fare, beer and wine, and non-alcoholic beverages from Coca-Cola. Visit Smalls Sliders for burgers, fries, and shakes, stop by Franky’s for a gourmet hot dog or sausage, and cool down with Frios Gourmet Pops. Stop by Hearsay’s festival tent for a cold beer or beer bucket or grab a michelada, wine, or beer from Gaspacho’s festival tent. Non-alcoholic drinks from Coca-Cola as well as pre-packaged snacks can be purchased at the Community Partner Concessions Booth, proceeds benefiting Levy Park and the event’s community partners. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Face Painting & Henna Art: Get into the tournament spirit with face and body art from Butterfly Faces and Henna Station & Glitter Bar Merchandise: Event merchandise celebrating Houston, Levy Park, and the global soccer tournament will also be available for purchase. Art Installations and Photo Opportunities: Commemorate the experience with a photo tour of the park, including life-sized soccer-themed photo backdrops and a tournament bracket. Visit our soccer ball music box and turn the crank for festive sounds. Festival Guidelines: VISITORS MUST COMPLY WITH DIRECTIONS FROM PARK PERSONNEL, OR THEY WILL BE ASKED TO LEAVE THE PARK. PARENTS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR CHILDREN’S SAFETY IN THE PARK. CHAIRS AND SEATING: No outside furniture. Blankets may be brought into the Festival site for the designated blanket seating area. All other furniture is available on a first-come, first-served basis. STROLLERS & WAGONS: Oversized strollers and wagons may need to be parked in a designated area during the festival. All visitors must comply with park personnel regarding stroller and wagon parking. FOOD AND BEVERAGES: Guests are permitted to enter with one factory-sealed bottle of water. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Other outside food and drinks are prohibited (exceptions will be made for baby food and necessary medical dietary food items). A variety of food, non-alcoholic drinks, beer, and wine will be available for purchase from Festival concessionaires. RE-ENTRY: If you leave the Festival site, you will be re-screened before re-entry. THE FOLLOWING ARE PROHIBITED: Smoking or Vaping Umbrellas Drug Use Kites and Drones Recreational Motorized Vehicles Guns, knives, any weaponry Soliciting Bikes, scooters, rollerblades, and roller skates

Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. item.title: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas (Late)
item.description:
Thursday, July 9, 2026 at 9:30 PM

Location: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino, 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV, 89103, United States

This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: Welcome to the Ion: An Introduction and Tour
item.description:
Friday, July 10, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Join the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, Wade Pinder, for an engaging tour and introduction to the Ion, Houston’s dynamic hub for innovation and entrepreneurship, powered by Rice University. This event is designed for entrepreneurs, students, professionals, investors, community leaders, and anyone curious about what the Ion has to offer. For those new to Houston and eager to connect with the local innovation ecosystem, this event provides the perfect opportunity to get started. The tour will begin in the lobby at 10:00 AM and conclude at 11:00 AM. During this time, participants will learn about the Ion’s resources, events, and facilities. Highlights of the tour include the technology showcases, coworking spaces, public areas, and the on-site restaurants and bars. About Wade Pinder Wade Pinder is a dedicated advocate for Houston’s innovation community, serving as the Ion’s Mentor in Residence. With a wealth of experience in product management, community building, and fostering entrepreneurial growth, Wade offers invaluable insights into how the Ion serves as a launchpad for ideas and innovation. The Vision of the Ion Powered by Rice University, the Ion is the epicenter of the 16-acre innovation district in the heart of Houston’s midtown. Committed to being the home for Houston’s innovation community, the Ion District propels the transformative culture of people, places, ideas, and experiences that build a better quality of life for all of Houston. The Ion is a beautifully restored building at 4201 Main Street. It connects Houston’s talent, academic, corporate, and entrepreneurial communities in a collaborative environment designed to inspire and grow ideas. The Ion serves as a space where serendipitous collisions lead to meaningful connections and opportunities. What to Expect Coworking Spaces: Explore flexible work areas tailored for collaboration and creativity. Public Spaces: Discover spaces designed for networking, inspiration, and community events. Restaurants and Bars: Experience the on-site dining options that make the Ion a lively hub. Through its programs and partnerships, the Ion empowers individuals and organizations to build, solve, and innovate. From prototyping to pitching, accelerating to sustaining, the Ion is Houston’s headquarters for turning ideas into reality. Whether you have a promising product, an intriguing technology, a budding business idea, or are simply curious about the Ion and its offerings, this tour will provide valuable insights into how the Ion can help connect your “What-ifs” with “What now.” Don’t miss this opportunity to explore and be inspired by Houston’s innovation ecosystem.

  Speaker: Debjeet Pathak Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences Location: Keith-Wiess Geological Laboratories The emergence and long-term habitability of Earth depend on the acquisition and redistribution of life-essential elements (LEEs), including C, N, P, S, H, and O, during planetary formation. This thesis investigates the chemical pathways that governed the origin, evolution, and delivery of these elements from the earliest stages of Solar System history to the formation of Earth. By integrating high-pressure-temperature experiments, meteoritic observations, geochemical reconstructions, and planetary accretion models, this work constrains the behavior of LEEs during core formation, planetary differentiation, and planetary growth. New experimental constraints on the partitioning of nitrogen and phosphorus between solid and liquid metallic alloys (Chapter 2 and 3), together with nitrogen partitioning between cohenite and metallic liquid (Chapter 4), are used to reconstruct the inventories of life-essential elements in the parent bodies of iron meteorites—the earliest differentiated planetesimals in the Solar System. Comparison of these reconstructed inventories with those of chondrites reveals the spatial and temporal evolution of life-essential elements during the earliest stages of Solar System formation and suggests that inner Solar system planetesimals were the major contributors of phosphorus and nitrogen to the growing Earth. Complementary electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) measurements significantly expand the existing nitrogen dataset for iron meteorites, providing improved constraints on their parent-body nitrogen inventories (Chapter 5). Furthermore, reconstructed zinc, sulfur, and gallium inventories provide evidence that disequilibrium condensation played an important role during the formation of these early planetary bodies (Chapter 6). Finally, numerical models of a Mars-sized last giant impactor demonstrate that its metallic core, rather than its silicate mantle, could have been an important source of volatile and life-essential elements delivered to the silicate Earth (Chapter 7). Collectively, this thesis provides new geochemical constraints on the origin, redistribution, and delivery of life-essential elements during planetary formation, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding the chemical pathways that ultimately led to Earth's habitability.   (Department : Earth, Environmental and Planetary Sciences)

item.title: Programmable control of small non-coding RNA expression in mammalian cells with synthetic RNA polymerase III transactivators.
item.description:
Friday, July 10, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: Keck Hall

  Speaker: Matthew Demelo Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: BioSciences-Biochemistry and Cell Biology Location: Keck Hall 102 Reliable control of gene expression via synthetic genetic circuits is essential to develop next-generation therapies, to facilitate efficient bioindustrial processes, and to enable advanced methods in basic cell biology. Synthetic control of small non-coding RNAs (sncRNAs) is of immense interest due to their important roles in development and disease in mammals, as well as their central role in technologies such as CRISPR/Cas gene editing and RNA interference. RNA polymerase III (Pol III) is the canonical polymerase for sncRNA expression, but few tools for regulated Pol III expression exist, requiring expression from RNA polymerase II (Pol II) promoters. While there has been extensive development of synthetic regulatory methods for expressing protein-coding RNAs and large non-coding RNAs via Pol II, these methods are often ineffective for robust expression of functional sncRNAs and often require post-transcriptional processing for sncRNAs to achieve functionality, impairing the feasibility of translating sncRNA technologies into medical and industrial applications. Here, I develop a toolkit capable of highly programmable and multiplexable expression of synthetic sncRNAs using Synthetic Pol III Transcription Factors (Syn3TFs), facilitating far more effective and robust expression of sncRNAs in mammals than previous methods. Additionally, I outline concise design rules for the construction of minimal Pol III promoters and complementary Syn3TFs, facilitating seamless construction of orthogonal Pol III circuits with customizable outputs. Finally, I demonstrate the utility of Syn3TFs in performing complex genetic logic and acting as efficient sensors for continuous molecular recording of cellular events. This platform represents a crucial first step to expanding the arsenal of circuit construction strategies for sncRNA expression and provides a strong foundation for continued development of Pol III-specific synthetic regulators.   (Department : BioSciences-Biochemistry and Cell Biology)

item.description:
Friday, July 10, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: Keck Hall

  Speaker: Matt Demelo Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: BioSciences-Biochemistry and Cell Biology Location: Keck Hall 102 Reliable control of gene expression via synthetic genetic circuits is essential to develop next-generation therapies, to facilitate efficient bioindustrial processes, and to enable advanced methods in basic cell biology. Synthetic control of small non-coding RNAs (sncRNAs) is of immense interest due to their important roles in development and disease in mammals, as well as their central role in technologies such as CRISPR/Cas gene editing and RNA interference. RNA polymerase III (RNAP3) is the canonical polymerase for sncRNA expression, but few tools for regulated RNAP3 expression exist, so genetic circuits requiring regulated sncRNA expression must use RNA polymerase II (RNAP2) promoters. While there has been extensive development of synthetic regulatory methods for expressing protein-coding RNAs and large non-coding RNAs via RNAP2, these methods are often ineffective for robust expression of functional sncRNAs and often require post-transcriptional processing for sncRNAs to achieve functionality, impairing the feasibility of translating sncRNA technologies into medical and industrial applications. Here, we develop a toolkit capable of highly programmable and multiplexable expression of synthetic sncRNAs using Synthetic RNAP3 Transcription Factors (Syn3TFs), achieving greater than 10-fold improvement in efficiency compared to analogous RNAP2-mediated methods. Additionally, we outline concise design rules for the construction of minimal RNAP3 promoters and complementary Syn3TFs, facilitating seamless construction of orthogonal RNAP3 circuits with customizable outputs. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of Syn3TFs in performing complex genetic logic and acting as efficient sensors for continuous molecular recording of cellular events. This platform represents a crucial first step to expanding the arsenal of circuit construction strategies for sncRNA expression and provides a strong foundation for continued development of RNAP3-specific synthetic regulators.   (Department : BioSciences-Biochemistry and Cell Biology)

item.title: Free Watch Party: Norway vs England (4pm) and Switzerland/Colombia vs Argentina/Egypt (8pm)
item.description:
Saturday, July 11, 2026 at 2:30 PM

Three days of quarterfinal madness wrap up tonight, and the stakes couldn’t be higher. By the final whistle, we’ll know our four semifinalists. Don’t miss the moment it all becomes clear. Kickoff for Norway vs England is at 4:00 p.m. Kickoff for Game 2 is at 8:00 p.m. Admission is free! Community Partners: Supporting this event is the Houston Show Choir. Houston Show Choir is made up of talented adult singers who perform an entertaining, diverse repertoire with lively choreography. They produce two big shows every year in June and December and perform at community events throughout the year. Their vision is “to share the joy of music”, if that resonates with you, auditions are in August and January! Email director@houstonshowchoir or follow us on Facebook/Instagram for more info! Face Painting & Henna Art: Get into the tournament spirit with face and body art from Gio’s Art Kreations and Henna Station & Glitter Bar Merchandise: Event merchandise celebrating Houston, Levy Park, and the global soccer tournament will also be available for purchase. Art Installations and Photo Opportunities: Commemorate the experience with a photo tour of the park, including life-sized soccer-themed photo backdrops and a tournament bracket. Visit our soccer ball music box and turn the crank for festive sounds. Festival Guidelines: VISITORS MUST COMPLY WITH DIRECTIONS FROM PARK PERSONNEL, OR THEY WILL BE ASKED TO LEAVE THE PARK. PARENTS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR CHILDREN’S SAFETY IN THE PARK. CHAIRS AND SEATING: No outside furniture. Blankets may be brought into the Festival site for the designated blanket seating area. All other furniture is available on a first-come, first-served basis. STROLLERS & WAGONS: Oversized strollers and wagons may need to be parked in a designated area during the festival. All visitors must comply with park personnel regarding stroller and wagon parking. FOOD AND BEVERAGES: Guests are permitted to enter with one factory-sealed bottle of water. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Other outside food and drinks are prohibited (exceptions will be made for baby food and necessary medical dietary food items). A variety of food, non-alcoholic drinks, beer, and wine will be available for purchase from Festival concessionaires. RE-ENTRY: If you leave the Festival site, you will be re-screened before re-entry. THE FOLLOWING ARE PROHIBITED: Smoking or Vaping Umbrellas Drug Use Kites and Drones Recreational Motorized Vehicles Guns, knives, any weaponry Soliciting Bikes, scooters, rollerblades, and roller skates

item.title: Introduction to Teaching the Holocaust
item.description:
Tuesday, July 14, 2026 at 9 AM

Location: Holocaust Museum Houston Classroom

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a one day workshop designed to help educators to feel comfortable teaching about the Holocaust. The day will include a tour of the museum’s Holocaust Gallery, a talk from a Holocaust survivor or descendant, best practices for teaching about the Holocaust, an overview of some of the free resources available, and more.  Breakfast and lunch will be provided. Teachers will earn 6 CPE hours and 6 GT update hours. Teachers from the 6th-12th grade, in all subject areas, are encouraged to participate in this FREE workshop. Sign up through the registration link below. If you have any questions about the workshop, contact us as education@hmh.org.    Interested in a more in-depth exploration of the Holocaust? We also offer the Max M. Kaplan Summer Institute for Educators, which includes pedagogical and content sessions from scholars and museum educators. You can find more information and apply here: https://hmh.org/education/professional-development/max-m-kaplan-summer-institute/. Register Here

item.title: Why Networking Isn’t Turning Into Deals — And What To Do Instead
item.description:
Tuesday, July 14, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1991195256614?aff=oddtdtcreator Networking is one of the most common business development activities in oil & gas, energy, and industrial sectors. But for many companies, networking is not consistently turning into real opportunities. You’re attending events. You’re meeting people. You’re having conversations. You’re building relationships. But the pipeline does not always reflect it. This session is designed to break down why networking often fails to convert into deals—and what companies can do differently to turn conversations into qualified opportunities and real business development momentum. Because networking alone is not a strategy. A strong relationship can open the door, but without structure, follow-up, and clear movement, opportunities often stall before they ever become real pipeline. What You’ll Learn Why networking alone does not create predictable growth The difference between visibility, conversations, and actual pipeline Where most companies lose momentum after an event or introduction How to follow up in a way that creates real opportunities How to turn relationships into qualified conversations and deal flow What a simple system looks like for moving from connection to opportunity Who Should Attend Oil & gas operators and service companies Energy and industrial organizations Executives, business development leaders, and sales teams Founders and operators responsible for growth Companies that attend events, conferences, and industry gatherings but want better conversion from those conversations Event Format 30–40 minute presentation 15–20 minute discussion and Q&A Optional networking following the session About the Speaker Jada Powell is the Founder of Powell Consulting Group, where she works with oil & gas, energy, and industrial companies to build structured, repeatable business development systems that drive consistent pipeline and revenue growth. Her work focuses on helping mid-market companies move beyond relationship-driven growth into more scalable, measurable commercial strategies. This session is part of The Pipeline Series: How Oil & Gas Companies Actually Grow Revenue, a monthly in-person series at The Ion focused on helping oil & gas, energy, and industrial companies create more consistent pipeline, stronger follow-up, and better conversion from conversations to revenue.

From Ion District

item.title: Free Watch Party: Semi-Finals Day 1
item.description:
Tuesday, July 14, 2026 at 12:30 PM

Two wins away from glory, and only two teams will get there. The semifinals are where World Cup dreams live or die — and we’re watching every breathless minute together. Kickoff is at 2:00 p.m. Admission is free! Food and Beverage Concessions: Enjoy a variety of festival food fare, beer and wine, and non-alcoholic beverages from Coca-Cola. Visit Smalls Sliders for burgers, fries, and shakes, stop by Franky’s for a gourmet hot dog or sausage, and cool down with Frios Gourmet Pops. Stop by Hearsay’s festival tent for a cold beer or beer bucket or grab a michelada, wine, or beer from Gaspacho’s festival tent. Non-alcoholic drinks from Coca-Cola as well as pre-packaged snacks can be purchased at the Community Partner Concessions Booth, proceeds benefiting Levy Park and the event’s community partners. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Face Painting & Henna Art: Get into the tournament spirit with face paint and body art from Butterfly Faces and Henna Station & Glitter Bar Merchandise: Event merchandise celebrating Houston, Levy Park, and the global soccer tournament will also be available for purchase. Art Installations and Photo Opportunities: Commemorate the experience with a photo tour of the park, including life-sized soccer-themed photo backdrops and a tournament bracket. Visit our soccer ball music box and turn the crank for festive sounds. Festival Guidelines: VISITORS MUST COMPLY WITH DIRECTIONS FROM PARK PERSONNEL, OR THEY WILL BE ASKED TO LEAVE THE PARK. PARENTS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR THEIR CHILDREN’S SAFETY IN THE PARK. CHAIRS AND SEATING: No outside furniture. Blankets may be brought into the Festival site for the designated blanket seating area. All other furniture is available on a first-come, first-served basis. STROLLERS & WAGONS: Oversized strollers and wagons may need to be parked in a designated area during the festival. All visitors must comply with park personnel regarding stroller and wagon parking. FOOD AND BEVERAGES: Guests are permitted to enter with one factory-sealed bottle of water. To go food from Kind Ice Cream, Hearsay, and Gaspachos is also welcome inside the festival site along with one factory sealed drink per person. Other outside food and drinks are prohibited (exceptions will be made for baby food and necessary medical dietary food items). A variety of food, non-alcoholic drinks, beer, and wine will be available for purchase from Festival concessionaires. RE-ENTRY: If you leave the Festival site, you will be re-screened before re-entry. THE FOLLOWING ARE PROHIBITED: Smoking or Vaping Umbrellas Drug Use Kites and Drones Recreational Motorized Vehicles Guns, knives, any weaponry Soliciting Bikes, scooters, rollerblades, and roller skates

item.title: Probabilistic Analysis of Nonstationary Hydroclimate Extremes
item.description:
Wednesday, July 15, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Ryon Engineering Building

  Speaker: Yuchen Lu Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Civil and Environmental Engineering Location: Ryon Engineering Building 112 Hydroclimate extremes, including extreme rainfall and tropical cyclones, pose substantial threats to communities, infrastructure systems, and ecosystems. Probabilistic characterization of these extremes is essential for risk assessment, infrastructure design, mitigation planning, and climate adaptation. Many commonly used approaches for estimating hydroclimate hazards assume stationarity, even though observations and climate projections show that extreme events are influenced by climate variability and long-term climate change. However, accounting for this nonstationarity poses methodological challenges: observations of rare events are sparse in time and space, while climate model products contain systematic biases. To address these challenges, this dissertation develops statistical frameworks that incorporate nonstationarity into probabilistic analyses of hydroclimate extremes using limited observational records.   The first chapter develops a hierarchical Bayesian space-time framework for nonstationary analysis of extreme rainfall probabilities. This framework mitigates the challenge of larger sampling variability and uncertainty by incorporating time-varying climate covariates and spatial pooling, allowing information to be shared across stations while estimating spatially coherent changes in daily extreme rainfall. The second chapter extends this analysis to multi-duration rainfall frequency estimates by incorporating duration dependence. This work addresses the challenge of maintaining coherence across both space and durations, which is especially important for short-duration rainfall extremes where observations are particularly sparse. The third chapter develops a nonstationary joint probability framework for characterizing tropical cyclone parameters relevant to hazard analysis. This approach mitigates the challenge of limited local tropical cyclone observations by using regional changes in storm characteristics to inform local-scale analyses and by linking dependent storm parameters through physically motivated relationships. Together, these three studies address a common problem in hydroclimate risk analysis: how to estimate changing extremes from limited and spatially heterogeneous observations. Across rainfall and tropical cyclone applications, the proposed frameworks improve the stability, spatial coherence, and physical interpretability of nonstationary hazard estimates. These methods provide a basis for more robust infrastructure design and climate adaptation planning under changing hydroclimate risk. (Department : Civil and Environmental Engineering)

item.title: Proton-Conductive Porous Solid Electrolytes for CO2 Electrolysis into Pure Liquid Products
item.description:
Wednesday, July 15, 2026 at 3:30 PM

Location: Ralph O'Connor Building

  Speaker: Abdullah Alazmi Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering Location: Ralph O'Connor Building 5th floor The carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) offers a promising route for converting CO2 into valuable chemical feedstocks, addressing both environmental and industrial needs. Achieving CO2RR electrolyzer devices that are highly efficient requires not only selective and stable catalysts for the reduction reactions, but also optimal device engineering, which includes ion transport between the cathode and anode sides of the electrochemical cell mediated by electrolytes. Despite the decreasing cost of renewable energy improving the viability of electrochemically produced feedstocks, the liquid fuels and chemicals produced through CO2RR are of low purity due to contamination from aqueous electrolytes collected with the products, increasing the overall cost of the products. This dissertation presents new classes of solid electrolytes that enable the operation of CO2RR reactors without the use of aqueous electrolytes, thereby minimizing the overall product cost by producing pure liquid products. This approach enables water to flow through the solid electrolyte layer while also transporting ions, mediated by the proton-conductive surface functionality. To address the broader challenge of solid electrolyte design, we investigated multiple material platforms, including mesoporous silica, electrospun polymers, and silica-polymer composite membranes to establish relationships between structure, porosity, and ionic conductivity. Among these materials, we demonstrate strong performance, achieving a high proton conductivity of 7.2 x 10-2 S cm-1 through sulfonated silica particles, significantly exceeding commercial solid electrolyte resins. These results highlight the effectiveness of nanoscale surface functionalization in enabling efficient proton transport while maintaining fluid pathways. This work establishes design principles for porous solid electrolytes and identifies promising platforms for enabling high-efficiency, contaminant-free CO2 electrolysis.   https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/6699460372?pwd=geShPhx3vChkVLk9HhWkOjMrgg5VW7.1&omn=97998132641 (Department : Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering)

item.title: Educating Traumatized Teenagers: The Extraordinary Story of a Swedish International School
item.description:
Thursday, July 16, 2026 at 6:30 PM

After World War II, Sweden absorbed and provided medical treatment for thousands of sick survivors. What to do about those who were teenagers, who had missed years of study on account of the war?  In September 1945, the Swedish government issued an order for schooling to be offered to those under the age of 18. In this presentation, Dr. Bernice Lerner will describe the complex process of recruiting wary adolescents, the challenges of teaching homeless, orphaned, and “environmentally damaged” teenagers, and instructors’ goals and methods at the most experimental of sites—the “Internat” school her mother attended. Dr. Bernice Lerner is the author of All the Horrors of War: A Jewish Girl, a British Doctor, and the Liberation of Bergen-Belsen, and other writings on the Holocaust and on virtue ethics. She is the former dean of adult learning at Hebrew College, former lecturer on the Holocaust at Boston University, and a senior scholar at Boston University’s Center for Character and Social Responsibility. Gerald S. Kaplan Endowed Lecture.

item.title: Mapping Houston's Innovation Ecosystem
item.description:
Friday, July 17, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 027, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002

Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it. Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration. The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights. This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth. Ion’s Vision Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey. From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem. Who Should Attend? This session is ideal for: Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources. Investors curious about the local startup landscape. Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community. Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship. Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene. Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem. Event Details 📅 Date:  Friday, March 21, 2025 ⏰ Time:  10:00am 📍 Location:  The Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

item.title: Cobalt Photocatalysis as a Platform for Tunable Hydrogen Atom Transfer in the Ring Opening of Cyclic Ethers
item.description:
Friday, July 17, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

  Speaker: Brian Funk Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Chemistry Location: BioScience Research Collaborative 1060 A/B This dissertation explores thoughtful design and development of synthetic methods photocatalyzed by Vitamin B12 and analogous cobaloximes. Central to these protocols is control over diverging HAT from Earth-abundant Cobalt complexes and simple organic thiols, shown to be heavily influenced by proticity of the reaction environment. Through strategic control of HAT directionality, these works provide mild, complementary reactive scaffolds to classical hydrogenation by hydride nucleophiles and carbonyl production by traditional Meinwald rearrangements. The addition of these new techniques to the synthetic chemist's toolbox has the potential to improve the limited accessibility of hydride-like reactivity in chemical synthesis, influence the perception of cyclic ethers as precursors to valuable functional handles, and further advance the onset of VB12 and its derivatives as powerful photocatalysts. Armed with the strong mechanistic foundation elucidated throughout this dissertation, further application of Cobalt photocatalysis in broader substrate classes can maximize the impact of this powerful, sustainable, and tunable reactivity.   (Department : Chemistry)

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: CCS Nerd Yard Sale III
item.description:
Saturday, July 18, 2026 at 10 AM

CCS Houston Nerd Yard Sale III — Dig In. Deal Out. Pass It On. Got shelves full of stuff that deserves a new home? Looking to score fan-loved finds at yard-sale prices? CCS Houston Nerd Yard Sale III is back for a full weekend — two days of clearing, digging, dealing, and connecting with fellow fans across every fandom and era. This isn’t a convention. It’s not a vendor hall. It’s a true community yard sale where real collectors clear their collections, real deals get made, and real conversations happen over shared fandoms.   📅 Date: Saturday–Sunday, July 18–19, 2026 ⏰ Time: Saturday: 10AM – 6PM | Sunday: 10AM – 5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 77036 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 🧺 For Sellers — Clear Your Shelves, Make Some Cash Got boxes of fandom stuff ready to move? Duplicates, impulse buys, collections you’ve outgrown? Set up a table, meet fellow fans, and pass your collection on to someone who’ll love it just as much as you did. Perfect for collectors downsizing, families clearing closets, and anyone who needs to make space. 👉 Apply to be a seller   🔍 For Shoppers — Dig, Deal, Discover Bargain hunters, this floor is yours. Browse tables packed with fan-loved finds at yard-sale prices across every fandom and era. You never know what you’ll find — but here’s what might be waiting: 📚 Comics, manga, and books 🎮 Retro games and consoles — NES, SNES, Sega, PlayStation classics, and more 🧸 Plushies, pins, keychains, and gacha 🧩 Anime merch, figures, and Funkos 📼 VHS, vintage media, and old-school collectibles 👕 Fandom fashion and accessories 🃏 Cards, toys, and unexpected gems Prices are yard-sale friendly. Every table is different. The best finds are the ones you didn’t know you were looking for.   👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 All Fandoms. All Ages. Zero Gatekeeping. Bring the whole crew. No pressure. No gatekeeping. Just fans connecting with fans over the things they love.   🏨 Traveling to Houston? Lock In Your Rate We’ve secured a special hotel rate exclusively for Nerd Yard Sale III attendees. Book your stay and make it a full weekend. 👉 Book here   Bring your trade boxes. Bring your shopping bags. Bring your inner treasure hunter. CCS Houston Nerd Yard Sale III — July 18 & 19.

From CCS Houston

item.title: Punk Rock Garage Sale
item.description:
Sunday, July 19, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: Bad Astronaut Brewery, 1519 Fulton Street, Houston, TX, 77009, United States

Insomnia Gallery and Deep End Records are excited to announce the date for our July Punk Rock Garage Sale! If you haven’t caught on yet, these happen on the 3rd Sunday of EVERY MONTH at Bad Astronaut brewing! While summer is heating up, stay relatively cool as this event is ***ALL INDOORS!*** and the event space itself now has AC! There will be OVER 50 VENDORS inside this massive adult playground of a venue which features pool tables, foosball, air hockey, cornhole and more (and all FREE to play!) We’ve got makers, artists, collectibles, thrift and vintage, music, books, video games, movies and vendors selling so much more! If you’re looking for a gift or to treat yourself, come to Insomnia Gallery’s Punk Rock Garage Sale for a true chance to score! NEW VENDORS EVERY MONTH! About this event:Based on the punk rock garage sales that took place regularly at Walter’s Downtown, Insomnia Gallery has been keeping this tradition alive for the last 6 years! DIY Forever! item.title: Angel Investing 101
item.description:
Tuesday, July 21, 2026 at 5:30 PM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 029 – 030, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

In a world where only the very wealthy, well connected, and major institutions have access to premium investment opportunities, which have created massive wealth for a small portion of the population, the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team believes the key to closing income and wealth gaps globally is to democratize access to opportunities across the investment ecosystem. Join the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team for an evening of learning, discussion and possibilities as we explore the basics of angel investing and the role it plays in bringing new products and services to market and the impact it has on wealth and job creation.. At this event, you’ll learn the key components to successfully navigate the critical-path of investing in private, early-stage companies. This session is ideal for the following investment related stakeholders: Prospective Angel Investors who want to learn more about the world of Angel Investing Investment Advisors (RIA/FA) who are looking for alternative investments for their clients Entrepreneurs who want to learn more about what Angels are looking for in their deals Entrepreneurs who want to meet/network with Angel Investors Ion District Investor Activation Program: The Houston Ion District Investor Activation Program along with Urban Capital Network is helping build an equitable climatetech industry capable of rapid deployment by addressing a fundamental challenge: the region’s lack of funding for early-stage climatetech startups, and especially for those led by underrepresented founders. This program from Greentown Labs and the Ion brings early-stage investors from Greater Houston—a region playing a pivotal role in the energy transition—into the fold, offering education on climatetech investing, channeling a pool of capital to young startups, and catalyzing a thriving climatetech investment ecosystem that prioritizes diversity, equity, and inclusion. If you would like to join the program, please fill out this form, and if you have additional questions, please contact Juliana Bernal Martinez at jbernal@greentownlabs.com.

From Ion District

item.title: NASA Tech Talks
item.description:
Thursday, July 23, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

We want HOU! Join us to discover NASA’s toughest tech challenges–and apply your skills and expertise to solve them.In these presentations, occurring the fourth Thursdays of the month, Mr. Montgomery Goforth and other aerospace subject matter experts will discuss the technology development challenges faced by NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the surrounding Aerospace community in our ongoing efforts as the hub of human spaceflight. Presentations will focus on the ways in which these challenges, and the associated opportunities, can be leveraged by Houston’s innovation community.Join us after the talk for drinks and networking at Second Draught!Past NASA Tech Talks have included: Montgomery B. Goforth discussing NASA Intellectual Property suitable for commercialization by small/start-up companies; Jared Daum discussing Orion’s parachutes and risk identification and mitigation that are showstoppers for the spaceflight parachute industry; Kevin Kobylka discussing current Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) capabilities and needs; and Nick Skytland, Chief Technologist at the Johnson Space Center (JSC) and Director of the Business Development and Technology Integration Office. Future NASA Tech Talks will include: dual-use (space/terrestrial) technologies in the areas of: Avionics / Communication / Sensors Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long lived wireless sensors Power Storage and Distribution Autonomous & Robotics Systems Extra-Vehicular Activity (EVA) Systems Virtual/Augmented Reality in Human Spaceflight Training & Execution Human Health & Performance / Human Systems Research About the Speakers Montgomery B. Goforth has more than 40 years of experience as both Engineer and Manager in a variety of highly technical space and defense-related efforts.  After working for a small defense contractor specializing in anti-submarine warfare, he joined NASA’s Johnson Space Center in 1990.  He has held leadership positions in multiple JSC Directorates and Program Offices. In his current role as Assistant Director of the JSC Engineering Directorate, he has established a framework to better focus Engineering’s efforts towards Human Spaceflight technology and systems development consistent with JSC and Agency goals for exploration. He has used this framework to guide Engineering’s internal investments and external partnerships supporting Lunar and Mars Exploration. Mr. Goforth was born in East Texas, raised in Southern California and Arizona, and graduated from Rice University (BSME 1982, MSME 1987). NASA Tech Talks topics include dual-use (space/terrestrial) technologies and focus areas in: Avionics / Communication / Sensors Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long-lived wireless sensors Power Storage and Distribution Autonomous & Robotics Systems Extra-Vehicular Activity (EVA) Systems Virtual/Augmented Reality in Human Spaceflight Training & Execution Human Health & Performance / Human Systems Research NASA Intellectual Property suitable for commercialization by small/start-up companies Orion’s parachutes and risk identification and mitigation strategies Leveraging Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long-lived wireless sensors

From Ion District

So, what is the difference between a cup of joe and a Cup of Joe-Y? It is the WHY. It’s not what you do. It is why you do it! item.title: Fourth Saturday Phenology Walk
item.description:
Saturday, July 25, 2026 at 9 AM

Fourth Saturday of the Month9:00 – 11:00 amFree, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Meet in front of the Nature Center building Discover the hidden seasonal rhythms of nature firsthand on our guided Phenology Walks, where we track the life cycles of different plants across ecosystems, from the first spring bud burst to winter dormancy. You’ll learn how shifting weather patterns and climate change influence the timing of these important events in our local ecosystems and how you can become a community scientist, contributing vital data from your own backyard to a global research initiative. These relaxing morning walks are led by scientists from Rice University and staff from the Arboretum. We welcome nature enthusiasts of all ages, however kids 12 years and younger must be accompanied by a guardian. Learn more about the study of phenology and ways you can contribute at https://www.usanpn.org/nn Community Science Partner

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson
item.description:
Wednesday, July 29, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: DiverseWorks – MATCHBOX 2, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Presented by DW Art + Climate Partners6:30 pm, Wednesday, July 29, 2026Suggested Ticket Price: $25 (pay-what-you-wish) Get Tickets10% of ticket sales will be donated to the Texas Tribal Buffalo Project The DiverseWorks Art + Climate Partners present Emily Johnson as the inaugural speaker for Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS. Join Houstonians, climate advocates, dance and art enthusiasts, and artists alike on the evening of July 29th for a talk by Johnson, a Yup’ik multi-disciplinary artist, choreographer, land and water protector, and organizer for justice, sovereignty and well-being. In October 2026, Johnson’s Overflow Radio will be presented at DiverseWorks. Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS highlights artists and creatives that are leading the way on addressing climate-related issues through their work. The DW Art + Climate Partners support and advise on climate programming and future projects. DiverseWorks’ Art + Climate program began in 2023-24 and consists of a climate action plan that guides the organization; programming that increases awareness of the effects of climate change; support for artists to develop environmentally sustainable practices; and the development of a new, climate-forward facility for artists, community members, and other non-profit organizations to share. Speaker BioEmily Johnson is a Bessie Award-winning choreographer, Guggenheim, Native Arts and Cultures Foundation, and United States Artists Fellow, and recipient of the Doris Duke Artist Award. She is based in Lenapehoking / New York City. Emily is of the Yup’ik Nation, and since 1998 has created work that considers the experience of sensing and seeing performance. Her dances function as portals and care processions, they engage audienceship within and through space, time, and environment — interacting with a place’s architecture, peoples, history and role in building futures. Emily is trying to make a world where performance is part of life; where performance is an integral part of our connection to each other, our environment, our stories, our past, present and future. Her choreography and gatherings have been presented across what is currently called the United States and Australia. Her large-scale project, Then a Cunning Voice and A Night We Spend Gazing at Stars is an all-night outdoor performance gathering taking place amongst 84 community-hand-made quilts. It premiered in Lenapehoking (NYC) in 2017, and was presented in Zhigaagoong (Chicago) in 2019. She choreographed the Santa Fe Opera production of Doctor Atomic, directed by Peter Sellars in 2018. Being Future Being, premiered on Tongva Land in Los Angeles in 2022. In 2011, DiverseWorks presented her performance The Thank-You Bar in conjunction with the exhibition This is Displacement: Native Artists Consider the Relationship Between Land and Identity (co-curated by Johnson and Diné visual artist Carolyn Lee Anderson).  Emily’s writing has been published and commissioned by The Open Society University Network’s Center for Human Rights and the Arts, ArtsLink Australia, unMagazine, Dance Research Journal (University of Cambridge Press); SFMOMA; Transmotion Journal, University of Kent; Movement Research Journal; Pew Center for Arts and Heritage; and the compilation Imagined Theaters: Writing for a Theoretical Stage (Routledge). Emily hosts monthly ceremonial fires on Mannahatta in partnership with Abrons Arts Center and Kai Recollet. She was the Pueblo Opera Cultural Council Diplomat at Santa Fe Opera 2018-2020, and a lead organizer of First Nations Dialogues. She was a co-compiler of the documents, Creating New Futures: Guidelines for Ethics and Equity in the Performing Arts and Notes for Equitable Funding, was a member of Creative Time’s inaugural Think Tank, and serves as a working consortium member for First Nations Performing Arts.

From DiverseWorks

item.title: NASA Stories at the Ion: Building the Moon Base: Challenges and Opportunities at the Lunar South Pole
item.description:
Thursday, July 30, 2026 at 8:30 AM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Building the Moon Base: Challenges and Opportunities at the Lunar South Pole In this presentation, Moon Base Principal Systems Engineer Shatel Bhakta shares the many challenges NASA must overcome to realize an enduring presence in the lunar South Pole region. He’ll also talk about his journey at NASA, the importance of human space exploration, and what NASA needs from the next generation of aerospace engineers. About the Speaker Shatel Bhakta serves as the principal systems engineer for NASA’s Moon Base. In that role, he takes a system-of-systems view of Moon Base infrastructure, ensuring that all components work together to support NASA’s goal of an enduring human presence in the lunar South Pole region. Prior to working on the Moon Base, Bhakta served as NASA’s lunar architecture lead, guiding a multidisciplinary team across NASA centers to develop a roadmap for crewed exploration of the Moon. This included developing associated conceptual reference missions, concept of operations, site planning guidance, trades and analysis, system element conceptualization, and system-of-systems integration. Bhakta earned his undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering from The University of Texas at Austin and his graduate degree in space architecture from the University of Houston. He is a licensed professional engineer in the state of Texas.  

From Ion District

item.title: Houston Restaurant Weeks 2026
item.description:
Saturday, August 1, 2026 at 12 AM

Houston Restaurant Weeks is the largest annual fundraiser for America’s largest food bank, the Houston Food Bank. It’s a month-long dining extravaganza featuring specially priced lunches, brunches, and dinners at restaurants from The Woodlands to Galveston. Participating restaurants make donations based on how many prix fixe brunches, lunches, and dinners they sell during the event. Diners are not solicited for donations. Beginning July 15, diners can visit HoustonRestaurantWeeks.com to view the 2026 list of restaurants that have committed to participate, along with their HRW menus. The event includes restaurants located in Harris, Galveston, and Montgomery counties. The Galveston County Food Bank and Montgomery County Food Bank are part of the Houston Food Bank’s Affiliate Food Banks. The Houston Food Bank provides food to these smaller food banks, which in turn distribute the food to hunger relief charities in a portion of HFB’s service area. The Houston Food Bank certifies that their Affiliate Food Banks meet Feeding America standards.

item.title: Houston Comic Exchange II
item.description:
Saturday, August 1, 2026 at 10 AM

Houston Comic Exchange II – Built for Comic Collectors Summer is prime comic-hunting season, and CCS Houston Comic Exchange II brings together collectors, dealers, and fans for a day of buying, selling, trading, and discovering comics. From key issues and first appearances to hidden gems and box-fresh finds, every table offers something worth digging for. No gatekeeping, no pressure, just comics and the people who love them.   📅 Saturday, August 1, 2026 | 10AM – 5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 📦 50 Vendor Tables – All Comics, All Formats Singles, back issues, key issues, first appearances, graded slabs, raw runs, indie and small press, variant covers. Vendor tables dedicated entirely to comics, no toys, no filler. If you’re a comic collector, this floor was built for you.   🔍 Key Issues and First Appearances This is where the hunt lives. Vendors bring the deep cuts, raw back issues worth digging through, graded books if you’re chasing condition, and the kind of keys that actually show up when serious collectors are clearing their own collections to make room.   📚 Back-Issue Digging and Indie Discovery Not every great find is a grail. Long boxes of back issues across decades and publishers, plus indie comics and small press titles that never make it to a standard shop shelf. Come with a list or come ready to browse – both work.   🤝 Vendors Who Collect Too The people behind these tables are the same people who will ask what you’re hunting before they start pulling books for you. The Houston Comic Exchange is a community floor first. The conversations are part of the event.   🛒 Vendor Table Applications Houston comic vendors: we’re gathering a focused comics-only crowd, and free entry is driving serious foot traffic. Apply for your table here 👉🏻 https://forms.gle/7q6pjcoiJTPbJouP8   The key issue you’ve been tracking is probably in one of those long boxes this summer. The Houston Comic Exchange II, August 1. Free entry, free parking, always.

From CCS Houston
